standard_prerequisites.name: Category
standard_prerequisites.statement: A category is a precategory whose hom-types are sets.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis under which the four conditions are compared, and the set-ness of the hom-types is what makes the fibers propositions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fiber of a function between sets
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a function between sets, injectivity is equivalent to all fibers being mere propositions.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the equivalence of conditions (1) and (3) at source line 138.

standard_prerequisites.name: Inhabited mere propositions are contractible
standard_prerequisites.statement: A mere proposition that is inhabited is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the step from condition (3) to condition (4) at source line 139.

core_obligations: Record that the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2) is standard category theory and does not need to be redone (source line 136).

Consider the function (f o blank) : hom_A(x,a) -> hom_A(x,b) between sets and observe that condition (1) says it is injective while condition (3) says its fibers are mere propositions, so the two are equivalent (source lines 137-138).
Derive condition (4) from condition (3) by taking k := f o g and using that an inhabited mere proposition is contractible (source line 139).
Derive condition (1) from condition (4): if p : f o g = f o h then (g, refl) and (h, p) both inhabit the contractible type of condition (4), so they are equal and hence g = h (source line 140).

proof_roadmap.step: Dispose of the standard equivalence and compare conditions (1) and (3) through fibers.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.1.1 at source lines 124-134: for a morphism f in a category, four conditions are equivalent, namely being a monomorphism, having the diagonal map an isomorphism, having all sigma-type fibers mere propositions, and having a contractibility property. The author's proof (source lines 135-141) is a cycle of implications in which each step uses a different fact: the standard equivalence with the diagonal condition is quoted (line 136), conditions (1) and (3) are identified by reading injectivity as propositionality of the fibers of the map (f o blank) between sets (lines 137-138), condition (3) implies (4) because an inhabited mere proposition is contractible (line 139), and (4) implies (1) by exhibiting two elements of the contractible type and concluding equality (line 140). The statement is a four-way equivalence and records neither the fiber translation nor which of the four steps consumes contractibility.
